data.narrative:
Fid Labs is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Adam Wolnikowski that has raised $1.7M to date. The valuation exercise benchmarks against a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though a narrow peer set of directly comparable seed-stage companies limits triangulation depth.

Stage-progression analysis, the primary applicable method, uses total capital raised ($1.7M, rounded to $2M proxy) as a baseline and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression in this sector, yielding $4M. Peer-median analysis was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics and manufacturing sector—only one same-stage peer existed, falling short of the three-point minimum for reliable median calculation. A broader peer median would risk distortion across heterogeneous company scales and business models.

The triangulated valuation range sits at $4M (low and median) to $5M (high), with a median point estimate of $4M. This reflects the single-method constraint: only stage-progression supplied quantitative grounding. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for Fid Labs' specific market dynamics, the company's unit economics relative to the broader comp set, and execution risk inherent to seed stage. Additional data on customer traction, burn rate, or product specificity would strengthen conviction in this range.
